single.rationale: NAPCO shows strong profitability metrics (26% operating margin, 28% FCF margin) and an attractive recurring revenue model (48% of revenue at 91% gross margin), but FY2025 showed concerning revenue decline (-3.8%), equipment sales weakness, and significant tariff headwinds affecting Dominican Republic manufacturing. The transition toward recurring services is promising long-term, but near-term execution risks and macro uncertainty warrant caution.

team.thesis: NAPCO operates a dual revenue model with recurring cellular communication services representing 48% of FY2025 revenue at 91% gross margin, but faces near-term margin pressure from a new 10% baseline U.S. tariff on products manufactured in the Dominican Republic using Asian-sourced materials, with management stating mitigation success is uncertain.

dropped.claim: NAPCO's recurring cellular communication services—representing 48% of total revenue with 91% gross margins and growing 44% from fiscal 2023 to fiscal 2025—provide high-quality earnings power that generated $51.4M in free cash flow (28.3% FCF margin) despite a temporary 3.8% revenue decline driven by $11.5M in door-locking product destocking and tariff uncertainty, positioning the company to resume growth as the dealer network restocks and the $3 billion school security market remains in early stages of adoption.

Equipment gross margin collapsed from 29.4% to 23.6% in FY2025, a compression of 580 basis points that represents a structural profitability problem in half the business. While the thesis emphasizes the 91% margin on recurring services, it ignores that the equipment business—which still generates approximately 52% of revenue—experienced severe margin deterioration that management has not explained or demonstrated ability to reverse.
